title: Smoothness Adaptivity in Constant-Depth Neural Networks: Optimal Rates via Smooth Activations
summary: Smooth activation functions are ubiquitous in modern deep learning, yet their theoretical advantages over non-smooth counterparts remain poorly understood. In this work, we study both approximation and statistical properties of neural networks with smooth activations for learning functions in the Sobolev space $W^{s,\infty}([0,1]^d)$ with $s>0$. We prove that constant-depth networks equipped with smooth activations achieve smoothness adaptivity: increasing width alone suffices to attain the minimax-optimal approximation and estimation error rates (up to logarithmic factors).
